dayIndicator.tooltip: Played on {weekday} in the tournament's local time ({location}). It appears on this day because the match finished on {userWeekday} in your timezone.
dayIndicator._tooltip_context: Tooltip on a finished-match chip on the matches-by-date list. Surfaced when the match's tournament-local date differs from the user-selected day-tab. {weekday} = full localised weekday name in the tournament's timezone (e.g. 'Saturday'), produced by Intl.DateTimeFormat with weekday:'long'. {userWeekday} = same, in the user's timezone. {location} = short tournament city/country (e.g. 'Asunción P2'). Both weekday placeholders are bare standalone words — translators should NOT prepend articles or prepositions that assume a particular grammatical gender (e.g. PT 'no' fails on feminine days like 'terça-feira'). Use neutral phrasing or commas instead.

stageChip._context: Chip on each tournament group header on the matches-by-date list, showing the most-advanced round happening on the selected day. Each tournament gets exactly one chip (Final wins over Semifinals if both are scheduled today). Qualifying covers Q1/Q2/Q3 collectively. Keep labels short — they sit next to a status pill (LIVE/ONGOING/etc.) and the chunky badge has limited width.

about.title: About Padel Nachos
about.tagline: Live padel scores with a side of fun
about.storyP1: Padel Nachos was born from a simple frustration. It was too hard to follow live padel matches. Scores were scattered across apps, social media, and official sites with no single place to get everything.
about.storyP2: We built PadelNachos to be that place. A fast, beautiful, free platform where fans can follow every point, every tournament, every player, from Premier Padel majors to FIP Gold events.
about.offerRankings: Official FIP rankings for men and women
about.offerDraws: Tournament draws and order of play
about.offerHighlights: Video highlights from top padel channels
about.dataP1: Our scores come from official tournament APIs and are verified against multiple sources. During live matches, data refreshes constantly to keep you as close to real-time as possible.
about.dataP2: We already track more than 3,000 players across men's and women's categories, and our database keeps growing every week.
about.disclaimer: Padel Nachos is an independent app for padel fans. We are not affiliated with or endorsed by Premier Padel, the International Padel Federation (FIP), Cupra FIP Tour, A1 Padel, or any professional player or league. Our goal is to make tournament information, live scores, and player profiles easier to access for fans of the sport. All player data and photos are sourced from publicly available APIs.

scorecard.title: The Path In — IOC Criteria

explanations.compliance: Padel meets all three IOC compliance frameworks: the Olympic Charter, the WADA Code (anti-doping), and the Olympic Movement Code on Manipulation of Competitions. This is a hard requirement and we're solidly past it.
explanations.continents: The IOC requires a sport to be practised on at least three continents. Padel is now played on five (Europe, Americas, Asia, Africa, Oceania), comfortably past the threshold.
explanations.federations: 87 countries have a national padel federation affiliated with the FIP. The IOC's general benchmark for global reach is around 75 federations — we're past that and growing every quarter.
explanations.gender: 40% of padel players globally are women. The IOC pushes hard for gender parity (50/50). We're on track toward that target — closing the last 10 points strengthens the case considerably.
explanations.elite: Only two countries — Spain and Argentina — currently have athletes capable of medalling at Olympic level. The IOC typically wants four or more countries genuinely competitive at the top before adding a sport. This is the biggest single gap in padel's Olympic case.

scorecard.blockerExplanation: This row is the single biggest obstacle to padel's Olympic inclusion. Every other criteria is met or on track — closing this gap is what padel needs most.

glossary.ioc: International Olympic Committee — decides which sports are in the Olympic Games.
glossary.fip: Fédération Internationale de Padel — padel's world governing body.
glossary.wada: World Anti-Doping Agency — sets the anti-doping standards every Olympic sport must follow.
glossary.noc: National Olympic Committee — your country's IOC-affiliated body. They vote on Olympic decisions.
glossary.aimag: Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games — multi-sport event in Riyadh, December 2026, where padel is now a medal sport.
glossary.brisbane2032: The 2032 Summer Olympics in Brisbane, Australia — the next opportunity for padel's Olympic inclusion.

why.title: Why we're tracking padel's road to the Olympics
why.intro: PadelNachos is a padel-first product. We are openly pro-inclusion. This page exists to help fans understand the path and to give them tools to support it.
why.stanceBody: We support padel's inclusion in the Olympic Games. We're not pretending to be a neutral journalism outlet — bias on the outcome is fine, sloppy on the facts is not.
why.rulesBody: Every counter on the tracker is linked to a primary source. When FIP says it, we link to FIP. When critical voices push back, they go in the Watchlist tab — not silently dropped.
